gloss: An apparatus composed of a wheel which spins inside of a frame (gimbal) and causes the balancing of the frame in any direction or position. In the form of a gyroscopic stabilizer, used to help keep aircraft and ships steady.
A swirling vortex.
A circular or spiral motion; also, a circle described by a moving body; a revolution, a turn.
Synonym of gyrus (“a fold or ridge on the cerebral cortex of the brain”).
An ocean current caused by wind which moves in a circular manner, especially one that is large-scale and observed in a major ocean.
A sports facility specialized for lifting weights, cardio machines, and other exercise (culturally differentiated from sense 1).
Physical education class (PE class).
A large room or building for indoor sports.
A type of secondary school in some European countries which typically prepares students for university.
A public place or building where Ancient Greek youths took exercise, with running and wrestling grounds, baths, and halls for conversation.
An itinerant person or any person, not necessarily Romani; a tinker, a traveller or a carny.

A move in contra dancing in which two dancers walk in a circle around each other while maintaining eye contact (but not touching as in a swing). (Compare whole gyp, half gyp, and gypsy meltdown, in which this step precedes a swing.)
A member of a Broadway musical chorus line.
A person with a dark complexion.
An insect, crustacean or bird literally having physical characteristics of both sexes, usually displaying a bilateral difference.
A person having certain physical characteristics of both sexes.
A philosophy and lifestyle based around the idea that nudity is a natural condition and should be widely acceptable in society.
A mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulphate. When calcinated, it forms plaster of Paris.
A style of Greek sandwich commonly filled with grilled meat, tomato, onions, and tzatziki sauce.
The act of turning or whirling, especially around a fixed axis or centre; a circular or spiral motion; rotation.
A rotation around an axis which is not the centre of rotational symmetry; an eccentric or off-centre rotation.
One of the whorls of a spiral univalve shell.
The arrangement of convolutions of gyri in the cerebral cortex of the brain.
Fear of or aversion to women or girls.
A moth of species Lymantria dispar, destructive of many plants, of worldwide distribution.
A sport involving the performance of sequences of movements requiring physical strength, flexibility, and kinesthetic awareness.
Complex intellectual or artistic exercises or feats of physical agility.
Any plant such as a conifer whose seeds are not enclosed in an ovary.
A member of the Romani people, or one of the sub-groups (Roma, Sinti, Romanichal, etc).
A member of other nomadic peoples, not only of the Romani people; a traveller. Alternative spelling of gypsy.
To shift a fore-and-aft sail from one side of a sailing vessel to the other, while sailing before the wind.
Of a fore-and-aft sail or its boom: to shift, often forcefully and suddenly, from one side of a sailing vessel to the other.
Generally of a small sailing vessel: to change tack with the wind crossing behind the vessel.
Often as gybe at: to balk, hesitate, or vacillate when faced with a course of action, plan, or proposal.
A sudden shift of a sail's angle, or a sudden change in the direction that a vessel is sailing in.
A manoeuvre in which the stern of a sailing vessel crosses the wind, typically resulting in the forceful and sudden sweep of the boom from one side of the vessel to the other.
A sudden change in approach or direction; vacillation.
An inordinate fear or hatred of nudity.
Any large falcon, especially as used to fly at herons.
Falco rusticolus, a large bird of prey that breeds on Arctic coasts and islands of North America, Europe and Asia.
A north-seeking form of gyroscope used as a directional reference in navigation.
of, relating to, or resulting from the properties of a spinning magnet, or a spinning electric charge; magnetogyric
Of or pertaining to gymnastics.
Of or pertaining to the gymnasia (ancient Greek schools).
The study of, or the branch of medicine specializing in, the medical problems of women, especially disorders of the reproductive organs.
Pertaining to, by means of, or in the manner of a gyroscope.
One who performs (the sport of) gymnastics.
A wandering monk having no fixed monastery, as exemplified in the Rule of St. Benedict.
Of or pertaining to gynecology.
Government or rule by women, or a society with such leadership.
An android (humanoid robot) in female form.
A fold or ridge on the cerebral cortex of the brain.
A triangular form having an angle at the fess point and the opposite side at the edge of the escutcheon.
Of or pertaining to women.
Of or pertaining to the female reproductive system.
Excessive development of breasts in men, resembling the breast development in women.
Having seeds that are not protected in a capsule
Of or pertaining to a gymnosperm
Containing gypsum.
Of a chalky white color.
The women's quarters in a household; (hence, loosely) any building or area for women.
An establishment in Rome where female workers made clothing and furniture for royalty.
A gynoecium.
Covered with gyrons, or divided into several gyrons, typically eight.
Attracted to women and/or to femininity regardless of gender.
Sexually attracted to women.
Sexually attracted to femininity, regardless of gender.
A man with gynecomastia.
Synonym of gymnospermous.
